properties.statement:
`Interface.medium` HAS NO VALUE FOR A CONTRACT BETWEEN INSTITUTIONS, AND `human` ABSORBED SEVENTEEN OF THEM. Reported by the US-government genesis session, 2026-08-15 (docs/feedback/2026-08-15-usgov-genesis-session.md, item 2), which graded it LOW and said so honestly: a workaround exists and is defensible.

MEASURED: `medium: \"process\"` for the presentment-and-veto boundary was refused with the full enum — `REST, gRPC, event, graphql, cli, library, data, mechanical, electrical, human, unspecified`. The session then used `human` for all seventeen check-and-balance interfaces and judged it defensible. Its objection is not that it was blocked: 'the enum reads as software-plus-hardware with `human` as an afterthought, and reflow2's own pitch is design anything. A constitutional procedure is not really a human-factors interface; it is a procedural or legal contract between institutions.'

WHY THIS IS RECORDED DESPITE BEING LOW, and it is a different argument from the reporter's: `medium` IS READ, not merely stored. The structural detectors use it — `library` and `data` earn the foundation exemption from `single_point_of_failure` (ver:interface-spec, tests/structural.rs), and `seam_report` compares it across paired designs, which is how a `medium` disagreement between two projects becomes visible at all. So seventeen boundaries filed under `human` are not merely mislabelled: they are being reasoned about as human-factors interfaces by every computation that reads the field. WHETHER THAT PRODUCES A WRONG ANSWER HERE IS NOT ESTABLISHED — no false single-point-of-failure was reported — but the field is an input to structure, not a label.

THIS IS THE SECOND DOMAIN TO PUSH ON THIS ENUM IN THREE WEEKS, which is the part worth noticing. `dec:the-mcp-surface-is-two-boundaries-not-one-medium` settled the FIRST push by SPLITTING an Interface rather than adding a value — Anthony chose that over introducing `json_rpc`, and the reasoning was that one Interface was describing two boundaries, not that the enum was complete. That reasoning does not transfer here: seventeen constitutional procedures are not one node describing two boundaries, and no split makes `human` mean 'procedural'. So this is genuinely new evidence about the enum rather than a repeat of a settled question, and the two pushes come from opposite directions — one wanted a PROTOCOL the enum lacked, this one wants a NON-TECHNICAL KIND it lacks.

CREDIT RECORDED BECAUSE IT IS ACTIONABLE EVIDENCE, not politeness: the session singled out the refusal message for listing every valid value, which made the fix a single retry. That is `req:a-refusal-names-what-would-have-worked` working in the field, on a first-time domain, reported by someone with no stake in it.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether `procedural`/`contractual` are the right words, whether a governance domain wants several values or one, and whether the enum should grow at all versus carrying an open string with a controlled subset. Enum values are NOT counted by the version stamp, so growing it is not a schema break.
